item.title: Here are 4 free agent OLs Kansas City Chiefs should consider signing
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs ' offensive line has put together lackluster performances in recent weeks as the perfect start to their 2026 campaign gave way to a two-game losing streak. While most of the talk about a blockbuster acquisition for Kansas City has centered around the Chiefs' need for a new wide receiver, fans shouldn't discount the team's potential interest in signing one or more offensive linemen as the NFL regular season approaches its midpoint. Here's a look at the five blockers who might be fits for Kansas City and are currently available in free agency: OT Taylor Decker Once regarded as one of the league's top tackles, Decker was released by the Detroit Lions earlier this year and still hasn't found a new landing spot. OT Jack Conklin Conklin earned first-team All-Pro honors in 2016 and 2020 but is still searching for work after suffering a season-ending concussion during his 2025 regular-season campaign with the Cleveland Browns . OT Jonah Williams A familiar foe of the Chiefs after his five-year tenure with the Cincinnati Bengals , Williams could bring some much-needed stability to the edges of Kansas City's front five. OT Cam Robinson Though he may be a better backup option than a starter for Kansas City, Robinson's experience could be a boon for the Chiefs if injuries further deplete the team's depth at tackle. item.title: Bill Simmons compares ‘insufferable’ Luka Doncic to Gordon Ramsay in latest rant
item.description: Credit: Dia Dipasupil/Chris Gardner/ via Getty Images Luka Doncic is enjoying a historic start to the 2026-27 NBA season, but Bill Simmons isn’t happy with one aspect of his game. Luka Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers have started the season winning six out of their first eight games. The Slovenian superstar has been playing on an unbelievable level, the numbers he is putting up are spectacular. Through seven games, Luka is averaging 38.3 points, 8.0 rebounds, and 8.1 assists per game. He is doing this while shooting 50 percent from the field, 43 percent from three-point range, and 89 percent from the free throw line. Despite all this, Bill Simmons thinks the Lakers star is ‘worse than ever’. Bill Simmons calls out Luka Doncic’s behaviour with referees, compares his ‘unhappiness’ to Gordon Ramsay One of the big criticisms that Doncic has faced in his career is his approach with the referees. In the past, he has received many a technical foul for complaining too much or doing it in a disrespectful manner. Luka has been called out for this numerous times, and spoken about wanting to improve. It seems that Simmons thinks that not only has Doncic not improved, he is apparently at his worst at the moment. He said as much during one of his latest podcasts, giving an unexpected analogy. “I think the guy is brilliant, I think he’s one of the best offensive players I’ve ever seen in my life,” Simmons said. “And it’s not a new take to say that his behaviour during games has been a little insufferable. I think this is the most insufferable he’s ever been. “I can’t believe how he behaves for 2.5 hours at these games and I don’t know one person who enjoys it. To me, it’s like when you see those commercials of Gordon Ramsay. Like, these reality chefs who are just screaming at everybody in the kitchen and you’re like, ‘Man it would s*** to work for that guy.’ “That’s Luka now in every game, he’s just unhappy constantly with everybody. And if somebody talks s*** to him on the other team, now he’s got to focus his rage on this… I’m just saying… I don’t want to put him on the Big TV because I don’t enjoy the process of watching him get those stats.” Many analysts have said similar things about Doncic in the past; Simmons certainly isn’t sharing a take which is unheard of. However, to do so at a point when the LA superstar’s game is speaking volumes more than any of his antics is a bit bizarre. item.title: Another Gauthier hat trick, Ducks hot power play payback Canucks
item.description: Nov 3, 2026; Vancouver, British Columbia, CAN; Anaheim Ducks forward Cutter Gauthier (61) celebrates after scoring a goal against the Vancouver Canucks in the first period at Rogers Arena. VANCOUVER, B.C. – Last Tuesday in Anaheim, it was an “unacceptable,” “terrible” and “careless” collapse to the last-in-the-league Vancouver Canucks. This Tuesday in Vancouver, there was another offensive surge, and despite a push from the hometown Canucks, the Anaheim Ducks rode history to a payback victory. Cutter Gauthier became the first player in Ducks history to net hat tricks in back to back games, as Anaheim’s historically hot power play unit buoyed a 5-4 road victory at Rogers Arena on Tuesday. Anaheim (7-7-1, 15 points) has scored 29 goals in the last five games and is 10 for 12 on the power play in the last three games. Ducks are the 10th team in NHL history to score three power play goals in three straight games and the first since the then-Mighty Ducks did it in March 2006. Anaheim’s 10 power play goals in three games is the most in the NHL since the 2008-09 Minnesota Wild, and Gauthier is the first player in NHL history with multiple power play goals in three straight games. Mikael Granlund opened the power play scoring, and after Vancouver evened on its own power play, Cutter Gauthier scored his first of two with the extra man. Leo Carlsson scored a shorthanded snipe for a 3-1 lead, and Gauthier’s second gave the Ducks a 4-2 lead into the third period. Gauthier ripped his third goal less than five minutes into the third period for his second consecutive hat trick and a 5-2 lead. Gauthier has scored goals in just four games this season, but each one has been a multi-goal night. He is the only the second player in Ducks history with three straight multi-goal games, joining Paul Kariya in 2000-01. Gauthier has eight goals in those last three games and is the first player age 22 or younger to do so since Patrik Laine in 1998 and just the second since Teemu Selanne in 1993. Beckett Sennecke assisted on all three Gauthier goals for his first career four-assist game. He is the fourth Duck in the last decade to register a four-assist game joining Ryan Getzlaf, Corey Perry and Nikita Nesterenko. Liam Ohgren scored the Canucks even-up power play goal, 1-1, and Linus Karlsson scored off a turnover to cut the Ducks lead to 3-2. Jake Debrusk scored on the power play and again at five-on-five in the third period to bring Vancouver back within one goal, 5-4. Laurent Brossoit stopped 19 of 23 shots in his second straight start as a Duck since being called up from AHL San Diego. Kevin Lankinen made 17 saves for the Canucks. Anaheim continues its three-game Western Canada road trip with the first half of a back-to-back in Edmonton on Thursday. The Ducks then play in Calgary on Saturday before returning home to host Pittsburgh next Sunday. Anaheim will debut its Hometown Remix jersey on Sunday against the Penguins. item.title: Amanda Serrano and Skye Falzon Face Off In Puerto Rico
item.description: What to Know Seven-division world champion Amanda Serrano confirmed her final fight will take place on January 9 in Puerto Rico at a news conference Tuesday. Serrano will face Skye Falzon of Australia in a 12-round fight with three-minute rounds in the main event of a Most Valuable Promotions card airing on DAZN Boxing . Serrano will attempt to break Christy Martin’s all-time knockout record in her final fight. After 18 years as a professional boxer, seven-division world champion and trailblazer Amanda Serrano has nothing left to prove as she makes a beeline for the Boxing Hall of Fame. But she will shoot for one last goal in her farewell fight on January 9 at the Coliseo de Puerto Rico in San Juan. Amanda Serrano arrives at the kickout press conference Tuesday in Puerto Rico announcing her retirement fight. Photo: Danny Mosaic, Most Valuable Promotions The historic event will mark the final professional fight of seven-division world champion Amanda “The MOAT” (Most Of All Time) Serrano (50-4-1, 32 KOs), who will defend her unified WBO and WBA featherweight world titles against Australia’s number four WBA contender Skye Falzon (12-2, 7 KOs) . Much like her longtime rival, Katie Taylor, Serrano will enjoy her last fight in front of her devoted fans on her island, a tribute she richly deserves, airing live on DAZN Boxing. At Tuesday’s kickoff event, Serrano and Falzon came face-to-face to discuss the highly anticipated showdown and the significance of Serrano’s final fight. Puerto Rico’s first and only undisputed boxing world champion will close her legendary career in front of her home fans, continuing her fight for equality in women’s boxing while seeking to break the all-time women’s knockout record. Serrano and Falzon were joined by Most Valuable Promotions founders and co-CEOs Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul for the official fight announcement in San Juan. “Back when MVP was just an idea and a promise to put fighters first, Amanda was the first athlete to believe in myself and my partner Jake Paul,” recalled Bidarian. “She entrusted us with her career, And she convinced us to go all in on women’s boxing. “Before she even met us, she was a seven-division champion. And since she’s met us, she’s added more belts. She’s become the first and only male or female undisputed champion in the history of Puerto Rico, she’s fought for equality and choice for women in the sport of boxing, including giving up her WBC belt to take a stand for three-minute rounds. She’s used her platform to push the next generation of male and female Puerto Rican boxers,” said Bidarian, noting that her dedication over 18 years has brought her to her final fight, being called “The Last Walk.” “We get to witness the greatness of Amanda Serrano on the last walk to the boxing ring. It’s going to be an incredibly loud and an incredibly emotional night, but above all, it will be a celebration of the most decorated boxer in the history of this great land,” said Bidarian. item.title: Alabama’s CFP ranking gets mocked on social media: ‘Legit insane’
item.description: The SEC had five teams in the top 12 of Tuesday’s first College Football Playoff poll, but social media wasn’t feeling Alabama at No. 5 . Kalen DeBoer’s Crimson Tide lost consecutive games to Georgia and Tennessee in October. However, wins over top-25 foes Kentucky and South Carolina apparently offset the losses along with the seventh most difficult schedule in the FBS, according to ESPN Analytics. RELATED : Why Alabama is ranked ahead of Tennessee “When you’re trying to compare teams head to head, they have to be in the same pod to be compared head to head,” CFP chair Hunter Yurachek said. “Alabama and Kentucky were in the same pod, they were compared because of their head-to-head matchup. Alabama got the nod ahead of Kentucky, because of that.” The ESPN analysts and social media didn’t really agree. “Doesn’t the committee realize Nick Saban is not at Bama anymore,” Danny Kanell posted on X. Alabama (6-2, 4-2 SEC) owns a road win in Week 2 over No. 6 Kentucky. That marks the Crimson Tide’s best win this season. The CFP also rewarded Alabama for the win over No. 21 South Carolina. The Crimson Tide’s two losses are to No. 2 Georgia at home and No. 13 Tennessee on the road. The Crimson Tide has a chance to add another road victory this week over a ranked opponent when it plays LSU on Saturday (2:30 p.m. CT, ABC) at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge. item.title: Corinthians celebrate first Brasileirão Under-17 title
item.description: Corinthians celebrate first Brasileirão Under-17 title Corinthians won the 2026 Brazilian U-17 Championship Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF Until this Tuesday (3), the Brazilian U-17 Championship trophy was still missing from Corinthians’ trophy cabinet. Not anymore. Despite a 3–1 defeat in Belo Horizonte, Timão secured the title thanks to their 3–0 win in São Paulo, winning 4–3 on aggregate. For Erasmo Damiani, Corinthians’ youth football executive, winning the Brazilian U-17 Championship reflects the efforts of the players and coaching staff throughout the season. “This achievement is incredibly inspiring. The coaching staff gave their all to help the players perform. It’s an undeniable achievement, because it’s our first national youth league title. It’s something much more special for everyone,” Damiani celebrated, referring to the club’s lack of titles in the Brazilian U-17 and U-20 Championships—Corinthians won the U-17 Copa do Brasil in 2016. The São Paulo side’s head coach, Guilherme Nascimento, explained that the title was the result of a process of connecting the players with the club’s “spirit and history.” “This title means so much. We worked hard with them on the pride and identity that come with wearing this shirt. Whenever Corinthians enters a competition, we need to be at the top. Today we managed to put Corinthians back at the top of Brazilian youth football. This is very important in everyone’s lives, and it will be a milestone in the careers of these players, who will go on to achieve so much more. This achievement is hugely significant for their development and for our work as a whole,” he said. Corinthians won the 2026 Brazilian U-17 Championship Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF Full-back Pedro Fernandes was instrumental in securing the title. item.title: Angels’ Ken Rosenthal reveals 1st move new owner Stan Kroenke must immediately make
item.description: Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images Angels’ Ken Rosenthal reveals 1st move new owner Stan Kroenke must immediately make appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Angels have renewed hope heading into the immediate future, as they are under new management after Arte Moreno’s disappointing 23-year stint as the owner of the franchise. Earlier this year, Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (KSE) purchased the Angels franchise from Moreno for a staggering $4 billion. This suggests that a better future is in the cards for the Angels, as the other sports franchises owned by KSE have been vastly successful in their respective leagues. And for MLB insider Ken Rosenthal, this is the first step family patriarch Stan Kroenke must make to kick off the rebuild in Anaheim after they won just 62 games in 2026. “If I’m Stan Kroenke, my first calls after I am approved as owner of the Los Angeles Angels would be to the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. The Brewers, to ask permission to interview Matt Arnold. The Rays, to request the same with Erik Neander,” Rosenthal wrote on his latest column for The Athletic. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Neither president of baseball operations would necessarily be interested. Both are under contract, so their respective teams might not even allow them to depart. So? The best way for the Angels to send a warning shot to the industry — one even more meaningful than signing free-agent left-hander Tarik Skubal — would be to lure away the architect of one of the World Series participants. Or at the very least, try.” Putting together a contending team starts by having the best minds in the business lead the franchise from the top. This suggestion from Rosenthal, as he so acknowledged, seems a bit ambitious, as the Brewers and Rays have been vastly successful over the past decade or so and aren’t just about to let one of the chief minds responsible for their success go without a fight. Nonetheless, this could be the way the Angels signal their intent to join the other KSE-owned franchises as champions. The Denver Nuggets (in 2023), the Los Angeles Rams (in 2022), the Colorado Avalanche (in 2022), and the English Premier League’s Arsenal (in 2026) have all won championships. It’s going to be a long road for the Angels, but they have to start somewhere .

item.title: With New Mexico Ranked, These Teams Have Yet To Make The AP Top 25
item.description: BOCA RATON, FL - FAU coach Lane Kiffen (right) speaks with FIU coach Butch Davis prior to the Owls' win on November 18, 2017, at FAU Stadium in Boca Raton, Florida. (Photo by Samuel Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images New Mexico has had its moments. Dennis Franchione’s 1997 squad, which included sophomore linebacker Brian Urlacher, won nine regular-season games before losing to Colorado State in the WAC championship and to Arizona in the Insight Bowl. Bob Davie’s team in 2016 won seven of its last eight to finish 9-4. Jerry Eck’s first season in Albuquerque a year ago also resulted in nine wins. An overtime loss to Minnesota in the Rate Bowl prevented a 10-win season, something only Joe Morrison’s 1982 squad accomplished. While Eck’s second season running the show might result in the program’s second double-digit win season, it has accomplished something Morrison’s squad, or any other at UNM, did not: an AP ranking. The first such ranking in program history went into the books Sunday when New Mexico checked in at No. 22 . (The Lobos are No. 25 in the coaches poll, which ranked them in 1997.) The AP poll was introduced in 1936 and New Mexico went 90 seasons and more than 1,000 weeks without a taste. item.title: St. Xavier, Sycamore take silver, bronze at state water polo tourney
item.description: Cincinnati's high school boys water polo teams had a strong showing at the Ohio state water polo tournament. St. Xavier finished as state runner-up, while Sycamore claimed third place in matches held on Oct. 31 at Sycamore High School. St. Xavier and Sycamore faced each other in the state semifinals, with the Bombers passing the Aviators in a 19-14 win. St. Xavier focused on shutting down Sycamore's star Ciaran Skinner with double-teams on defense, then using a balanced offensive attack that saw six Bombers score goals. St. Xavier went on to face Upper Arlington in the state finals, but couldn't quite finish the job in an 11-6 loss. Senior Spencer Meier had a standout performance from the center guard position, allowing zero goals defensively while scoring once and assisting on another goal. Senior goalie Lucas Mijares made multiple impressive saves in the first half to keep the Bombers competitive with the Golden Bears. It was the third consecutive appearance in the state semifinals for St. Xavier, but just its first trip to the finals since 2016. The Bombers' season wrapped up at 22-16-1 overall, recording a third-place finish at the Ohio Cup and a top-eight placement at Philadelphia's Beast of the East Tournament. Sycamore, who entered the tournament as the No. 7 seed, made a statement win in the quarterfinals. The Aviators knocked off defending champions St. Charles, who had only lost three times in 2026, in a 9-6 battle. Senior Colin McAllister earned a full line in the contest, while senior David Parker was the unsung hero in denying the Cardinals' 2-meter player any space to initiate the offense. Following their loss to St. Xavier in the semis, Sycamore knew it had a physical matchup with Thomas Worthington coming up. The two teams had faced off three times this season, with each being decided by a single goal and one player suffering a broken nose. After a back-and-forth three quarters, the physicality got the better of Thomas Worthington as two key players were fouled out or ejected. Sycamore won the final quarter by four goals, winning the match 16-12. Sycamore senior Ciaran Skinner, a first-team All-Ohio selection, made history in the state tournament. His 163 goals set a new single-season goal record, eclipsing the previous mark of 156. He scored 18 goals over four games in the tournament, also adding six assists, 23 steals, and 14 ejections drawn. item.title: Luka Doncic outdoes Michael Jordan, LeBron James and Nikola Jokic combined in staggering NBA stat
item.description: Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images Luka Doncic has set himself apart from some of the greatest players in NBA history after the Los Angeles Lakers highlighted an incredible statistical achievement from the Slovenian superstar. The Lakers revealed that Doncic has recorded 31 games with at least 40 points, 10 assists and five rebounds before turning 28. Michael Jordan, Magic Johnson, LeBron James and Nikola Jokic have managed just 23 such performances combined at the same age. The latest milestone comes after Doncic delivered another outstanding display in a 138-117 victory over the Miami Heat, finishing with 42 points, 13 assists and seven rebounds. Luka Doncic continues remarkable scoring run as Los Angeles Lakers beat Miami Heat Doncic’s performance also caught the attention of Giannis Antetokounmpo, who offered an extraordinary assessment of the Lakers guard’s scoring ability. Speaking after the game, the Milwaukee Bucks star suggested Doncic could be the greatest scorer basketball has ever seen. “Obviously, he’s one of the best scorers to play this game, if not the best,” Antetokounmpo said. When asked to clarify whether he meant currently or across NBA history, Giannis doubled down: “Not right now. Of all time. I feel like some people are scared to say that, but he’s got to be up there.” Doncic is certainly making a strong case with his performances this season. He is averaging 38.3 points per game, the highest mark in the league, while the Lakers have made a 6-2 start. His scoring average is also supported by a remarkable run of form. Doncic has averaged 43.4 points across his last five games, including consecutive performances of 45 points against the Toronto Raptors and 42 against Miami. Doncic’s career scoring average of 29.35 points per game is already the third-highest in NBA history, behind only Jordan and Wilt Chamberlain. With the Lakers winning games alongside his individual brilliance, Doncic’s challenge now is to maintain this level throughout the season and turn his historic start into a genuine championship push. Now, years after he played his last NFL game in 2010, Owens is opening up about why he was often perceived as the bad guy during his playing days, and he points to one critic in particular. Now, as Owens discusses his upcoming documentary titled “Terrell & T.O.” on his “ Get TO The Point Podcast ,” he believes fans will get to see a different side of him. “I think people are going to get a true understanding, because of the title itself, it differentiates Terrell from T.O.,” Owens explained. “What a lot of people know of me now, they just know T.O., right? The media, I ain’t gonna say, created that character, that person, but they put a target on that individual, T.O. That’s part of the theme of me being everybody’s No. 1 target. item.description: The Naugatuck High boys soccer team poses with the championship banner after defeating Watertown 3-1 on penalty kicks to win its third straight Naugatuck Valley League championship Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, at Municipal Stadium in Waterbury. The Greyhounds outscored the Warriors 3-1 on penalty kicks to win a game that seemed like a rollercoaster ride to all involved. It finally ended when Naugatuck's Deric Eshaghi made his penalty kick and set off a big celebration for the Greyhounds (15-1-3). "The feeling is unmatched. Right when we scored the (last) penalty, I started crying. I was fist-patting other guys that were crying," said Naugatuck senior captain Antonio Guerreiro, who was named the tournament's most outstanding player. "I couldn't wish for a better night. These boys, we worked so hard for this, all season. We worked so hard. Watertown gave us a great challenge, 3-3. I'm just so happy we could be here and win this game." item.title: A birthday at Diamante sparked a dream: How First Tee is changing lives in Los Cabos
item.description: LOS CABOS, Mexico – On the southern tip of Baja California Sur, where the Sea of Cortez meets the Pacific Ocean, a young girl discovered something that would change her life. Her name was Paloma Orozco. In 2024, Orozco attended the third round of the World Wide Technology Championship at Diamante's El Cardonal course as a member of First Tee Diamante. She enjoyed the experience so much that she asked her father if she could return for the final round the next day. There was one catch: Sunday was her 13th birthday. Her father, Diamante's head of security, couldn't say no. What followed became a turning point. Watching PGA Tour professionals up close, golf was no longer simply a sport she had been introduced to a few months earlier. "Something in my mind changed and I fell in love with the sport," Orozco recalled. But Orozco's story is about more than a young golfer discovering a passion. It is also a story about vision, community and the power of opportunity. That vision began with Jim Panoff, who splits time between Dallas and his home at Diamante. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Panoff realized that many children of Diamante employees had little or no access to golf. His grandson participated in First Tee in Texas and, during a Thanksgiving visit home, suggested that his grandfather start a chapter at Diamante. Panoff listened. He approached 25 original club founders and homeowners and asked each to contribute $25,000 in seed funding to launch First Tee Diamante, creating opportunities for local children through golf while teaching values such as perseverance, respect and confidence. Asked to describe First Tee in one word, Orozco didn't hesitate: "Happiness." Six years later, First Tee Diamante serves approximately 150 children ages 6 to 18 with the help of 40 Diamante staff members who volunteer as coaches. A bus transports participants to the Oasis Short Course, where they receive instruction, breakfast, lunch and daycare until 5 p.m. The program also sponsors junior tournaments throughout Los Cabos. "I think of this as the spearhead of youth golf in Cabo," Panoff said. Like martial arts' belt system, participants progress through different levels and wear the corresponding colored shirts, pants and ball caps. Younger children begin with SNAG equipment and advance through color-coded divisions such as yellow and orange before donning red and earning the opportunity to play traditional golf. The most accomplished players move into the elite black division, reserved for juniors who demonstrate both strong golf skills and academic achievement. They receive additional instruction focused on strategy and advanced techniques.
